title: Pricing your work, showing it, and growing steadily

say: Pricing your work, showing it, and growing steadily.
This is the video for module four of Basic Tailoring and Garment Repair.
Many beginner tailors guess their prices, or copy the cheapest person on the street. Then they work hard and have nothing left.

say: A price must cover four things. First, materials: the zip, thread, buttons. Count only what this job uses. One reel of thread does many jobs.

panel.heading: What a price is built from

say: Second, labour. That is the minutes you spend, times a fair value for your time per hour. Use the same hourly value every time.

panel.heading: What a price is built from

say: Third, running costs: fuel or electricity, needles, oil, data, transport. Add them for a month and divide by your usual number of jobs. For example, about 12,000 naira a month across about 60 jobs is about 200 naira per job.

panel.heading: What a price is built from

say: Fourth, profit, often 20 to 30% for small service work. Profit is not your pay. Your pay is already in labour. Profit lets you save, replace tools and grow.

panel.heading: What a price is built from

say: For example, Funke repairs clothes from home in Abeokuta. These prices are approximate, so use your own market prices.
Materials: the zip is 500 naira and thread about 50, so 550 naira.
Labour: about 45 minutes. At 1,500 naira an hour, that is 1,125 naira.
Running costs share: about 200 naira. So her total cost is 1,875 naira.
Profit at 20% adds 375 naira.
Her price comes to 2,250 naira. Nearby tailors charge between 2,000 and 3,000, so she rounds to 2,500. She knows she is not working at a loss.
Charge extra for same-day work, because it pushes other jobs back. A small discount for bulk work, like ten school trousers for one family, is fine.
Write prices as from a figure, so you can charge more for difficult fabrics. And time your jobs. You will get faster.

panel.heading: Charge fairly, never at a loss
left: Time each job and write it down

say: Never discount below your total cost. If you undercut a neighbour, you lose money on every job. Compete on quality, speed and reliability instead.
And check every transfer in your own app before handing over the garment.

say: Set up WhatsApp Business. It is free. Add a clear profile, a catalogue item for each service with a photo and a from price, and quick replies for your price list.

Meet in daylight, tell someone where you are going, never post your home address.

say: Look for partners. For example, Patience in Port Harcourt shows her photos to a dry cleaner and collects repairs twice a week. She gets steady work without advertising.

say: Your capstone proves you can do the work. Sew two buttons, one invisible hem, one zip, one seam or tear repair, one fit alteration, and one simple made item.

Each job needs a job card, before-and-after photos, a quality check and a costing. Add two feedback notes, an honest reflection, and a 90-day plan in three stages. To earn the certificate, you also need at least 70% in the final quiz.

panel.heading: Your capstone jobs
items: One pillowcase, apron or tote bag

say: Your practice: cost three services and write your price list, set up WhatsApp Business, visit one partner near you, and complete your capstone.
Now continue with the lessons below.
